note: The CLASS-first detection recipe: which generic evaluator a sink kind selects. A sink argument's kind (the same `kind` the models/ catalog stamps -- command-injection, alloc-size, weak-crypto, ...) routes to one of a CLOSED set of evaluators. Adding a catalogued kind that maps to an existing evaluator adds a whole detection category with no engine code; only a genuinely new evaluation primitive needs code. Pure data; no engine coupling -- an engine reads `kind_evaluator[kind]` and dispatches. The three evaluators are a documented vocabulary, not data the engine keys on beyond the closed set.

evaluators.reachability: Injection / traversal. An attacker-controlled value reaching the sink argument IS the lead -- the argument carries no length obligation, so taint alone fires. (command/sql/xss/ssrf/path/...)
evaluators.relational: Size / memory. The delivered length must be BOTH attacker-influenced AND unbounded relative to the destination capacity. Either alone is normal (a bounded tainted length; an unbounded constant). No taint -> no lead.
evaluators.presence: Configuration weakness. The CALL ITSELF is the defect regardless of taint (weak crypto, insecure TLS, predictable temp file). Collected per-call and fires even with constant arguments; taint is not consulted.
